subject: AtlasOps: SDK & API versioning — proposed timeline and next steps
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@atlasops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Product Team <product@atlasops.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SDK/API deprecation concerns and asks

Hi Marissa —

Quick background: AtlasOps relies on the Redwood JS and Python SDKs in our control plane integrations. We just completed an internal security review and the engineering team flagged the upcoming v1->v2 API shape changes (parameter renames, streaming payload restructure, and a new auth header format) as potentially breaking for clients who consume lower-level streaming frames.

Can you share: 1) confirmed deprecation timeline for v1 endpoints, 2) whether Redwood will maintain a compatibility shim for streaming frames, and 3) migration docs for the SDKs? Our product roadmap assumes stability through Q3, so we need to align ASAP.

Also looping in AtlasOps Legal for any contract/change-control concerns.

Thanks —
Samira Khan
Head of Partnerships, AtlasOps

---
Attachment: AtlasOps_API_change_proposal.pdf (summary of AtlasOps integration points)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@atlasops.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SDK/API deprecation concerns and asks

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the heads-up and for the detailed proposal. We take compatibility seriously and want to make this low-friction for partners. High-level answers:

- Deprecation timeline: we are proposing a 26-week migration window for v1 once we announce the deprecation (targeting a formal announcement end of Q2).
- Compatibility shim: engineering is evaluating a streaming compatibility layer for a subset of frame types; we'll confirm feasibility in our internal sync today.
- Migration docs: we will produce an SDK migration guide + code samples and a compatibility matrix.

I'd like to schedule a 45-minute roadmap sync to walk through the proposed changes, the MAP, and the handoff to your eng/legal teams. Are you available Wednesday 02/25 or Thursday 02/26? I'll attach an initial mutual action plan and a compatibility matrix after our internal conversation.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Partner Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_AtlasOps_MAP_v1.docx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: internal: AtlasOps compatibility asks

Marissa/Vivek/Laura —

Summary of the engineering take after a quick review:

1) Breaking changes identified: rename of `max_tokens` -> `token_limit` in some endpoints, streaming JSON envelope restructure (we move to chunked objects with meta headers), and auth header migration from `X-Redwood-Key` -> `Authorization: Bearer` (we are consolidating across infra).

2) Suggested partner-safe rollout:
   - Maintain v1 endpoints for 26 weeks after announcement.
   - Provide a compatibility shim that translates v1 streaming frames to v2 envelopes for common frames (chat messages, function call frames). Shim will be available in hosted API for 26 weeks; SDKs will include a client-side opt-in adapter for on-prem/dedicated customers.
   - Semver: bump major version for SDKs (2.0.0) and mark the adapter as a separate package (redwood-sdk-stream-adapter) with its own minor versions.

3) Docs/automation: generate automated migration samples, a compatibility matrix (see attached), and a test harness partner can run against staging to validate behavior.

Estimate: 3 engineer-sprints to implement shim + SDK adapter, 1 sprint for docs and migration samples. Risks: dedicated/private deployments where customers run older infra will need the client-side adapter + feature-flagging.

Happy to present technical details on the partner sync.

—Rishi
Director, Platform Engineering

---
Attachment: SDK_compatibility_matrix.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@atlasops.com>, Product Team <product@atlasops.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, AtlasOps Legal <legal@atlasops.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T18:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: AtlasOps: SDK & API versioning — proposed timeline and next steps

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the patience. Following our internal alignment, attached is a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and the compatibility matrix. Key points:

- We propose an official deprecation announcement on 2026-06-30 with a v1 shutdown date of 2026-12-31 (26-week window).
- Redwood will maintain a hosted compatibility shim for the full 26 weeks and publish an optional client-side adapter package for Dedicated/Private setups.
- SDKs will be released as major v2 versions with migration guides and code samples. We will provide staged test harnesses in our partner staging environment (url in the MAP).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm which AtlasOps teams need staging access and a preferred date/time for the sync (02/25 or 02/26).
2) Legal: if you have specific contract change requests related to deprecation SLAs, please flag them so we can align on an amendment.

I'll set up the calendar invite for 02/25 at 10:00 AM PT pending your confirmation.

Talk soon —
Marissa
Senior Partner Manager | Redwood Inference
